title: Devilled Kidneys
subtitle: Victorian spiced lamb kidneys on toast
excerpt: One of the great dishes of the Victorian breakfast table: lamb kidneys quickly fried in butter with Worcestershire sauce, mustard, and cayenne until just cooked and served on thickly buttered toast. Takes ten minutes.

recipe.sourceNotes: Devilled kidneys were a staple of the Victorian and Edwardian British breakfast table, part of the elaborate 'full breakfast' served in country houses and gentlemen's clubs. The word 'devilled' refers to the spiced, piquant seasoning common to Victorian cookery, typically involving mustard, Worcestershire sauce, and cayenne pepper. The dish fell out of fashion in the twentieth century as offal consumption declined in Britain, but has seen a revival in modern British cooking as appreciation for nose-to-tail eating has returned. The key technique is to cook the kidneys quickly over high heat; prolonged cooking produces a rubbery, strong-smelling result. The kidneys should be pink in the centre when served.

content.text: Prepare the kidneys just before cooking: remove the skin, halve them, and cut out the white fatty core with scissors. Cook over the highest possible heat in very hot butter; they should sizzle aggressively. No more than 2 to 3 minutes per side; they should be pink in the centre. Overcooking kidneys produces a strong, unpleasant result.

items.preparation: halved; white core removed; patted dry

content.text: Mix the mustard, Worcestershire sauce, and cayenne together in a small bowl.

Heat the butter in a heavy frying pan over very high heat until it is foaming. Season the kidneys with salt and pepper. Add them cut-side down and fry for 2 to 3 minutes without moving until browned. Turn and fry for 1 to 2 minutes more.
Reduce the heat. Add the mustard mixture and toss to coat. Add the lemon juice. Taste and adjust the seasoning. Pile onto the buttered toast, scatter with parsley, and serve immediately.
